newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Other Randgold mines may refine own gold.
newsitem.headline: Other Randgold mines may refine own gold.

text.p: Other South African gold mines in the Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd stable are likely to follow the example of Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd and refine their own gold, commercial director Brett Kebble said on Thursday.

Kebble said Durban Roodepoort Deep Ltd was likely to have a refinery in due course which would also handle material from West Rand neighbours Buffelsfontein Gold Mining Co Ltd and Blyvooruitzicht Gold Mining Co Ltd.

Plans for the East Rand mines were less advanced but Kebble said it was possible that a joint refinery would similarly be established for Grootvlei Proprietary Mines Ltd and East Rand Proprietary Mines Ltd (ERPM).
No final decisions on the new refinery projects had yet been taken but Kebble told Reuters "if we were to proceed it would certainly be in the next 18 months".

Harmony, which is building South Africa's first independent gold refinery, on Thursday became the first mine to win approval from the Reserve Bank to be allowed to sell some of its own production direct, rather than through the Reserve Bank.
The Randgold unit received permission to market internationally a third of its output, amounting to eight tonnes a year.

"It's clear it is going to be possible to market gold direct and it might be possible to achieve a higher price than is obtained through the Reserve Bank, so it must have merit on the that basis," Kebble said.
Harmony managing director Bernard Swanepoel said he hoped the mine would eventually be allowed to market its full production of around 24 tonnes a year.
Randgold mines produce in total around 50 tonnes of gold a year, or 10 percent of national output.
At present all mines refine their gold at the Rand Refinery -- the world's biggest -- which is collectively owned by the industry.
But Harmony announced last year it planned to break ranks by establishing its own commercial-scale gold refinery, which should be completed in the third quarter of 1997.

Harmony calculates it will be cheaper to refine its own gold than using the Rand Refinery. It says the cost of establishing the plant and acquiring new technology will be 3.3 million rand which is less than the annual savings it expects to achieve by smelting and refining its own gold.
